title: Adaptive Rate Limiter + Batch Token Metering and Quant Profile Seeder
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: We observed unit-econ regressions on spiky workloads where aggressive batching + static rate limits caused token-level cost overruns and cold-KV cache thrash. This PR introduces an adaptive token-rate limiter at the batch scheduler boundary paired with lightweight metering for token-prefill usage and a small quant-profile seeder that suggests tenant-scoped quantization presets based on early workload signals. Motivation: provide an automated safety net that keeps latency SLOs while reducing per-token cost for multi-tenant workloads and give operators a low-friction way to bootstrap quant profiles for new tenants. What changed: 1) runtime/batcher: add adaptive_token_rate_limiter which monitors per-second token consumption, outstanding KV cache hits, and recent decode latency to dynamically adjust allowed tokens-per-second for new micro-batches; 2) telemetry: emit token_meter.{tenant,route,model} counters and a prefill_efficiency gauge that feeds Optimize heuristics; 3) optimizer/quant: add quant_profile_seeder service that ingests short-lived telemetry windows and proposes quant presets (int8/int4/ffn-compression candidates) to the profile store; 4) policy: fallback rules so when latency or error signals spike the limiter aggressively reduces batch token budgets and favors lower-quantization safety tiers. Backwards compatibility: opt-in via feature flag "adaptive_batch_rate_v1" with default off for Dedicated/Private; telemetry schema additions are additive. Security/privacy: no model weights or request payloads are shipped; only aggregated token counts and micro-batch level latencies are emitted. Testing & validation: unit tests for limiter/hysteresis, integration test with local serving runtime that simulates spike traces, and an end-to-end smoke run against a staging tenant. Related Linear/Jira: ENG-4201 (adaptive limiter design), ENG-4202 (quant seeder prototype), SUP-1337 (incident that prompted throttle). Checklist: - [x] Design doc updated - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Docs/ops note added - [x] Feature flag gated - [x] Telemetry hooks added Migration notes: operators should enable the flag in staging for 24–72h to collect seeder suggestions before enabling in production. Rollout plan: canary 5 tenants -> 20% traffic -> 100% after 72h stable metrics.
commit_summary: 3 commits: 1) add adaptive_token_rate_limiter with hysteresis and config knobs; 2) wire telemetry and feature-flag gating; 3) implement quant_profile_seeder and CLI export of suggested profiles
review_conversation: Diego: 'Limiter looks sensible but add a guard for KV evictions — we saw regressions in a previous patch.' Asha: 'Added eviction-aware backoff and unit test (limiter_test.go).' Lena: 'Telemetry protobuf needs a stable name; prefer token_metering.v1.' Asha: 'Renamed and kept backward additive changes.' Ravi: 'Please ensure seeder proposals are advisory only and not auto-applied.' Asha: 'Seeder defaults to 'suggest' mode; applied only via admin approval; added CLI to export suggestions for review.' Approvals: Diego approved (2026-03-01), Lena approved with comment (2026-03-02), Ravi requested one minor change (made).
release_notes: Introduce adaptive token-rate limiter to control batch token budgets under bursty traffic; add token-level metering telemetry and a quant profile seeder that proposes per-tenant quant presets. Feature gated behind 'adaptive_batch_rate_v1'.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag in staging for 24-72h. Watch prefill_efficiency and token_meter.{tenant} counters. Seeder suggestions are exported to /var/lib/redwood/quant_suggestions/<tenant>.json by default. If latency increases, disable the flag to revert to static batch budgets.
testing_summary: Local unit tests cover limiter hysteresis and eviction backoff. Integration simulated scenario with 3x traffic spike and validated limiter throttles new micro-batches within 120s. End-to-end smoke on staging tenant showed 12% reduction in per-token infra cost with stable p95 latency.
notes_for_engineering: Telemetry fields are additive; downstream Optimize pipelines will consume token_metering.v1. Quant seeder outputs a ranked list of safe->aggressive presets. Be conservative when auto-applying presets; the PR keeps manual approval for now.
impact_assessment: Low risk when gated. Expected positive cost delta for bursty workloads where prefill inefficiency was >20%. No breaking API changes. Operational overhead: small additional telemetry ingestion and a background seeder job that runs every 15 minutes.
audit_log: PR created 2026-02-25 by Asha Patel. CI green 2026-03-03. Merged 2026-03-05 by Diego Moreno (squash).
